sourceRegistry.title: How Oracle turns days of work into minutes with ChatGPT and Codex
sourceRegistry.factSummary: OpenAI’s Oracle customer story describes staff using ChatGPT Work and Codex for research and business questions. Reported time savings are customer examples, not a guarantee for every task; people remain responsible for outputs.

sourceRegistry.title: Disrupting AI-enabled “false front” operations
sourceRegistry.factSummary: OpenAI reports banning accounts linked to two covert influence operations. One used fabricated journalist identities to submit articles. These findings concern identified operations, not all online writers or AI-assisted text.

concepts.title: Ask who and where
concepts.explanation: Meen asks “who”. In meen katab el-maʾaal?, katab is “wrote”. Feen asks “where” and often comes after the noun in a short question. No separate word for “is” is needed.

concepts.title: Make sure of something
concepts.explanation: Learn netʾakked men as a complete phrase: “we check / let’s make sure of”. Men introduces what you check. Lissa mesh means “still not”; a female speaker says metʾakkeda, and a male speaker says metʾakked.

sentences.english: Anna: I am looking for a piece of data.
Bence: I will ask a colleague.
Anna: How much time is needed?
Bence: Two minutes.
Anna: Here is the report.
Bence: Thank you, I will check the data.
Bence: I have a question.
Anna: What is the question?
Bence: Is this number correct?
Anna: I do not know yet.
Bence: I will look at the report.
Anna: Good, I will answer after that.

example.english: I am looking for a piece of data.
This is a piece of data.

concepts.title: Looking for something; checking a specific thing
concepts.explanation: Keresek is used here with an unspecified object: egy adatot, “a piece of data”. Ellenőrzöm is used with a specific object: az adatot, “the data”. Both objects take -t; the verb ending also reflects whether the object is specific. Learn the complete short phrases.

examples.english: I am looking for a piece of data.

concepts.title: Ask how much time is needed
concepts.explanation: Mennyi idő kell? means “How much time is needed?” After a number, Hungarian normally keeps the noun singular: két perc, “two minutes”. Kell expresses a need here; it does not change in these short examples.
